---
title: "Extend the Network"
---

The OPDI Sensor Network grows through partnerships. There are two ways to contribute to expanding open ADS-B coverage: working with the PRC to place sensors at strategic airport locations, or joining the OpenSky Network as an independent receiver operator.

## Place a Sensor at a Strategic Airport

The PRC deploys ADS-B sensors at airports where coverage is limited or nonexistent in the OpenSky Network. These placements are coordinated with airport operators, ANSPs, and local partners to ensure optimal positioning for ground-based and low-altitude surveillance.

**What we provide:**

- ADS-B receiver hardware (compact, low-maintenance)
- Integration with the OpenSky Network infrastructure
- Technical support for installation and configuration

**What you provide:**

- A suitable location at or near the airport (rooftop, tower, or similar with line-of-sight to the runway/taxiway area)
- A power supply and internet connection
- A local point of contact for maintenance

If you are an airport operator, ANSP, university, or aviation organisation with access to a strategic airport location, we would welcome your partnership.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Get in touch
Contact us at [pru-support@eurocontrol.int](mailto:pru-support@eurocontrol.int) to discuss placing a sensor at your airport.
:::

## Join the OpenSky Network

You can also contribute to open aviation data independently by setting up your own ADS-B receiver and feeding data to the [OpenSky Network](https://opensky-network.org/). The OpenSky Network is a crowd-sourced initiative — anyone with a receiver can participate, and the data benefits the entire research community.

**Getting started:**

- Visit the [OpenSky Network feeder page](https://opensky-network.org/contribute/improve-coverage) for instructions on how to set up a receiver
- Receivers can be built from affordable hardware (e.g., Raspberry Pi with an SDR dongle) or purchased as ready-made units
- Feeders receive access to the OpenSky Network API in return for their contribution

Every additional receiver improves the global coverage of open ADS-B data — whether at an airport, along a flight corridor, or in a region with sparse coverage.
